comment: Provenance for every package in forks/. bin/pi-setup-doctor reads this to report upstream drift; bin/pi-setup-vendor reads it to re-vendor a fork onto a newer upstream release. An entry with upstream:null is first-party and has neither. version is what a fork is BUILT ON; reviewedAgainst is a newer release that was read and deliberately declined, which suppresses the drift note for that one version only - the release after it reports again.

pi-dynamic-workflows-safe.note: extensions/workflow/index.ts imports ../../src/*.js, so src/ is the tree Pi loads. dist/ is a compiled mirror reachable only through the package exports field; rebuild it with npm run build.

pi-process-monitor-safe.note: Hand-written rewrite rather than a patch of upstream, imported with its original commit history. Not re-vendorable with bin/pi-setup-vendor. Reviewed against upstream 1.3.0 on 2026-07-30: every applicable fix was already present independently (poll-tick overlap guard, idempotent stop, coalescer cancel on teardown, spawn-error cleanup, watcher removal from state). Reviewed against upstream 2.0.0 on 2026-08-02 and DECLINED as a base, porting one fix. 2.0.0 is built on crash-safe persistence: logical watcher UUIDs, source fingerprints, lifecycle revisions, cross-process leases with boot-id/PID validation, restart quarantine, checkpoints, GC, and monitor_inspect/monitor_recover/monitor_gc to drive it. This fork deliberately persists nothing, so adopting 2.0.0 would mean reversing its central design decision, not upgrading it. PORTED: the per-tick poll timeout. The fork's no-overlap guard had no bound, so a poll child that never exited (a hung SSH, the exact case poll mode exists for) held the guard forever and the watcher went permanently silent. A tick now gets intervalMs-1000 and is killed via the existing process-group escalation, reported once through the existing failure latch. Reproduced before the fix. DECLINED, with reasons: suspension after N consecutive failures, because a suspended watcher strands an agent that is waiting on it and this fork has no recovery path to un-suspend it; exponential backoff with jitter, because retrying every interval means the watcher self-heals the moment a remote returns, and up to 5 minutes of extra detection latency is worse than some wasted cheap spawns on a multi-day run; poll confirmation and mutating-command quarantine, because the model already holds an unrestricted bash tool, so gating monitor commands moves no boundary; structured process/file/SSH/HTTP probes and process receipts, which are new surface area serving the persistence model. Revisit if this fork ever grows persistence. Reviewed against 2.0.2 on 2026-08-18. Releases 2.0.1-2.0.2 only migrate upstream's seven-source persistent monitor schema to a strict-mode-safe discriminated source object and preserve its legacy calls through prepareArguments. This fork exposes only three non-persistent modes (spawn, poll, tail), does not opt its extension tool into strict constrained sampling, and has no structured probe placeholders or recovery options for a decoder to fabricate, so there is no runtime fix to port. Revisit the discriminated schema if strict constrained sampling is enabled for this tool.

pi-btw-side.note: First-party extension, not a fork. Implements Codex's /side (alias /btw): an ephemeral fork of the conversation shown in a full-screen view that hides the main thread while it stays running. The npm packages named pi-btw and pi-render-btw are unrelated overlay implementations and are not installed. No upstream to track.

pi-setup-maintenance.note: First-party, skills only: no extensions and no tools. Carries the update-pi-setup skill, which documents the pinned update path for Pi, agent-browser, and every fork. Nothing to re-vendor.

unslop.note: First-party, skills only: no extensions and no tools. Carries the unslop skill, adapted from cursor/plugins with the Adding Soul section removed and the process reduced to three steps. Nothing to re-vendor.

pi-context-handoff.note: First-party extension, not a fork: replaces pi-continue. Steers Pi's own compaction, cannot abort a turn, and includes a mid-run fold of the request. No upstream to track and nothing to re-vendor.
